title: Correctness of the step scan
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $s$ be a natural number, and let $C$ be a configuration of $N$ on input $x$ whose work-tape heads and nonblank cells lie within distance $s$ of the origin. Let $a$ be an action and let $A'$ be a Boolean word of length $W_N(2s+1)$. The scan’s acceptance flag is true exactly when $A'$ is the encoded sequence of cells of the configuration obtained by applying $a$ to $C$ across the window of width $2s+1$, and the resulting configuration still has all work-tape heads and nonblank cells within distance $s$ of the origin.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
$C$ is a machine configuration on input $x$
All work-tape head positions of $C$ have absolute value at most $s$
Every work-tape cell of $C$ outside the interval $[-s,s]$ is blank
$A'$ is a Boolean word of length $W_N(2s+1)$
